title: Lighting an open-plan office
subtitle: BSE3125 Optics and Lighting | Mini lighting design exercise | Semester 1, 2026/27

sections.title: Design basis and spatial interpretation
paragraphs: The proposal provides maintained electric lighting for ordinary office paperwork, typing and data processing. It combines recessed 600 mm module luminaires with a fixed proposed arrangement of 112 desks in 28 four-person benches. Furniture positions are design assumptions because the supplied architectural drawing does not define the office workstations. The adopted task criterion is 500 lx average maintained illuminance, uniformity Uo >= 0.60, maximum directional UGR <= 19 and colour rendering Ra >= 80 [1,2].

The original DWG is retained unchanged. The selected office is the L-shaped interior around the northern service core. Office-facing wall lines, rather than the opposite core wall faces, define the boundary. The measured gross polygon is 1042.10 m2; deducting the eight source-linked column intersections gives 1032.57 m2. The drawing also contains a 1022 m2 annotation. That annotation is not treated as a boundary measurement; its smaller area is used conservatively only in the lighting power density check. Door gaps at the core boundary are bridged and the core is excluded.

The design assumes a 2.8 m ceiling, 0.8 m desk plane and 1.2 m seated eye level. Ceiling, wall and floor reflectances are 80%, 70% and 20%; columns are 40%. These are specified finishes rather than measured existing values. The model represents an electric-light condition with no daylight contribution. Facade glazing is not identified sufficiently for a daylight model, so opaque walls are assumed for this calculation. Confirm actual glazing and finishes before using the design for construction.

Each desk is 1.6 x 0.8 m. Benches retain at least 0.9 m clearance to walls or columns and at least 1.8 m between bench footprints. These planning clearances do not constitute an accessibility or escape-route certification. No high partitions, cabinets or monitor screens are modelled as opaque solids; changes to those obstructions require recalculation.

sections.title: DIALux workflow and calculation method
paragraphs: The architectural DXF establishes the scale and ceiling grid. The office contour and eight full-height columns are reconstructed as native geometry. Material reflectance, ceiling height, working planes and maintenance factor are specified before importing manufacturer photometry. A 3D review checks the spatial relationship between the recessed luminaires, room surfaces and columns. Geometry input alone is not a lighting result: every reported performance value comes from an actual DIALux calculation and its native output [3].

A single coordinate dataset links all 186 fixtures to their source ceiling tiles and persistent fixture IDs. The same coordinates generate the independent CAD layout and luminaire schedule. Native report coordinates are converted from the room frame and matched one-to-one against the shared dataset. This prevents the drawing from describing a different installation from the simulated model.

All 112 desk areas are calculated individually, rather than selecting only favourable desks. Directional UGR is assessed at 1.2 m eye height with a 0.4 m offset above the desk plane, over 0-360 degrees in 15-degree steps. The maximum reported value across desks and directions is used. The catalogue UGR label and the software's rectangular-room estimate are not substituted for these project-specific results.

Immediate surrounding areas extend 0.5 m around each bench activity area. Adjacent desks within a bench are themselves task areas, so the bench perimeter defines the surrounding band. Background illuminance is checked on the remaining office floor outside those expanded bench footprints. Cylindrical illuminance is assessed at seated head height over tasks and their surroundings. Exposed wall and ceiling evaluations exclude actual physical obstructions, with their evaluation-region coverage verified separately.

The model uses a fixed maintenance factor of 0.80, so reported illuminance is maintained rather than initial illuminance. Results are calculated in DIALux, saved, closed and reopened before final evidence is accepted. Native project, manufacturer assets, editable drawing and full raw reports remain separate from the compact submission PDF.

sections.title: Luminaire selection and ceiling coordination
paragraphs: The selected luminaire is Philips PowerBalance gen2 RC461B 34S/840 SEIA W60L60 VPC U4 WH SC UE, order code 910505103630. Manufacturer ULD and LDT files provide the actual intensity distribution; the native import gives 3400 lm and 19.8 W per fixture. The manufacturer leaflet rounds rated input to 20 W. The conservative power budget uses 20 W, while the native calculation retains the imported 19.8 W value [4].

The 4000 K source and Ra above 80 suit ordinary office visual tasks. The low-glare optic was selected after a higher-output CoreLine option exceeded the adopted directional UGR limit. The PowerBalance catalogue UGR value of 16 is useful for product screening, but glare acceptance uses the actual office calculation. Manufacturer flicker declarations are PstLM 1 and SVM 0.4; these are product declarations, not quantities independently measured in this project.

The nominal 600 mm module is coordinated with the source ceiling grid. The manufacturer physical body is 597 x 597 x 82 mm; the imported photometric geometry has a different depth representation. The native placement reference is 2.868 m, while the recessed emitting face is approximately at the 2.8 m ceiling. That reference coordinate must not be interpreted as a suspended visible mounting height. Provide a compatible ceiling support and sufficient plenum clearance for the full manufacturer body, driver and service access.

Every luminaire is assigned to a complete ceiling tile. Fixture L120 is locally moved one 600 mm module south to improve the desk that failed after grid snapping. The independent formal lighting plan includes all fixture IDs, simplified symbols, legend and product schedule; it is not a screenshot or CAD-window export from DIALux.

sections.title: Iteration and spatial performance
paragraphs: The first 142-fixture CoreLine arrangement illustrates why a whole-room average can be misleading. Its general working-plane average was about 501 lx, yet diagnostic desk averages were 479 and 516 lx and directional UGR reached 20.3. Raising surface reflectance improved useful interreflection but did not alone resolve glare. Replacing the optic with PowerBalance reduced glare, although retaining 142 luminaires gave insufficient desk illuminance.

Increasing the PowerBalance arrangement to 186 luminaires achieved the task targets before ceiling-grid alignment. Snapping the fixtures to actual tiles then reduced Desk-084 to 497 lx. The final local movement of L120 raised that desk to 557 lx. After this refinement, all 112 proposed desk areas pass the adopted task criteria: minimum desk average 504 lx, minimum desk Uo 0.80 and maximum directional UGR 17.5. These are extrema across different desks, not a single representative desk.

Desk-021 controls average illuminance: 504 lx average, 446 lx minimum, 541 lx maximum and Uo 0.88. Its 4 lx average margin is small and is reported explicitly. Desk-084 controls task uniformity, with 557 lx average, 445 lx minimum, 627 lx maximum and Uo 0.80. Desk-018 controls directional glare, with UGR 17.5 at 180 degrees. The native task plots and calculation tables in the appendix show their distinct spatial conditions.

The very low minimum on the original automatic whole-room workplane occurs in regions occupied by opaque columns; it must not be presented as the uniformity of usable desks. Conversely, excluding physical obstructions is not permission to discard dark occupied locations. All proposed tasks remain in the assessment. The additional surrounding, background and exposed-surface checks require complete coverage of their declared physical regions.

The accepted task results apply to the proposed fixed furniture and finish assumptions. The small critical illuminance margin makes accurate reflectance, maintenance and installation verification important. Recalculate if ceiling height, glazing, furniture, partitions, luminaire output or tile positions change. A complete guideline conformity claim would additionally require confirmation of the actual occupancy context and the specified commissioning provisions.

sections.title: Controls, power and operation
paragraphs: The control proposal defines 32 independent local zones: 28 bench zones and four circulation zones. Each zone has a local manual on/off/dim interface as well as automatic control; occupancy sensing does not replace the manual interface requirement. Every fixture belongs to exactly one zone. The largest zone is 46.67 m2, below the adopted 250 m2 automatic-control limit. The proposed 32 manual points meet the unreduced BEC Table 5.5 basis; no low-LPD reduction in that count is claimed [5].

Specify vacancy switch-off after 10 minutes, calendar shutdown for non-working periods and local timed overrides expiring within 120 minutes. Vacancy operation reduces power to zero. Wireless Interact-compatible group control and the selected sensor-equipped luminaires provide the proposed control route. Confirm actual sensor coverage at 2.8 m and group programming during commissioning; a functional diagram is a design provision, not evidence that the installed controls have been tested.

Provide daylight-responsive dimming where facade review establishes qualifying daylight zones. Final window geometry is not available, so no daylight contribution or energy saving is credited here. The absence of a daylight calculation is not a claim that the real office has no windows or that daylight-control clauses do not apply.

The conservative connected budget is 186 x 20 W plus a 50 W external-control allowance, giving 3770 W. Dividing by the smaller annotated area of 1022 m2 gives 3.689 W/m2, below the adopted BEC 2024 office limit of 7.2 W/m2 for areas above 200 m2. The native 19.8 W photometric inputs give 3682.8 W; the budget deliberately uses the larger datasheet value and an additional allowance. Confirm final controller and accessory loads against the scheduled products.

The native software's generic annual energy estimate is not used as an office-specific savings prediction. Actual annual consumption depends on working hours, occupancy, daylight and user operation. Control benefits are therefore described functionally rather than as an unsupported percentage saving.

sections.title: Maintenance, screen comfort and verification
paragraphs: The fixed maintenance factor is justified as 0.90 lumen maintenance x 1.00 survival x 0.95 luminaire cleanliness x 0.94 room-surface maintenance = 0.8037, rounded down to 0.80. L90 at 50,000 hours is manufacturer-declared; survival, cleanliness and room-surface factors are explicit design assumptions, not measured manufacturer values. Specify annual optical cleaning, prompt spot replacement of failures, three-yearly room-finish inspection and repainting as needed. Review illuminance after fit-out and revise the maintenance plan for actual soiling and operating hours. The manufacturer also declares L85 at 100,000 hours; this does not alone establish the complete installation maintenance factor [4].

Assume ordinary positive-polarity office displays with tilt no greater than 15 degrees. A bounded check of the manufacturer LDT samples gives a maximum average luminaire luminance of 1134.23 cd/m2 over gamma 65-89 degrees, below the conservatively adopted 1500 cd/m2 category. This is a sampled screening calculation. It does not establish the unmeasured angular maxima or the 90-degree endpoint, where a flat aperture has zero projected area. It is separate from room UGR, and it does not certify the full display-screen clause. Avoid direct reflected luminaire images on screens; use matte finishes and review screen orientation after furniture installation [2].

Commissioning should verify installed product identity and output, exact tile positions, emitting-plane height, room finishes, desk positions and maintained illuminance. Check directional glare from actual seated views, display reflections, vacancy timing, manual interfaces, override expiry and daylight response. Record deviations and recalculate affected areas. BEC 2024 is adopted as the academic design benchmark; statutory applicability also depends on the actual building and project timing, which the assignment does not specify.

The engineering evidence chain binds source drawings and manufacturer files to the shared design dataset, saved native simulation, reopened results and independent CAD plot. Original inputs are fingerprinted and preserved. The appendix contains selected original DIALux pages with their content unchanged; full raw outputs and editable sources remain available separately.
